To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

intensional failures in natural language data base query systems may be due to the user’s assumption of non-existent relations and that appropriate forms of corrective behavior may be designed which will enable the user to reformulate his/her queries in such a way that the system may be able to respond.

(a) the user of a data base query system may be unable to express his/her query in a manner that is consistent with the knowledge representation of the system; and (b) the system should be able to recognize such inconsistencies and to correct the user's query so as to enable him/her to express it in a consistent fashion.

intensional failures in natural language interactions with data base systems can be attributed to misconceptions regarding the domain of interest, and that these misconceptions can be recognized by the system and the user corrected.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an interactive system that will recognize and respond appropriately to intensional failures on the part of users in order to improve the effectiveness of the interaction.
the design of a natural language data base query system that is capable of detecting and correcting intensional failures on the part of its user.

the design of a data base query system that will provide the user with an opportunity to discover and rectify his own misconceptions and to make effective use of the information available in the data base.

the failure in a query system is due to the user's inability to formulate queries compatible with the knowledge base.

the failure of natural language processing in the context of data base query systems is not a result of the limitations of the natural language processing techniques, but is rather a result of the failure of the user to provide the system with the information necessary to solve the task.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the development of natural language systems is dependent on the development of knowledge representation schemes that are appropriate for the particular domain of discourse and for the particular task to be accomplished.
a natural language system can be used to help users formulate more precise and effective queries by detecting and correcting their failures in knowledge of the domain.
a significant class of failures can be attributed to misconceptions and incomplete knowledge on the part of users.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the user's task is not necessarily to retrieve information from the data base, but to use the information to solve a problem.

the knowledge representation and the user's knowledge of the domain of discourse must be taken into account in the development of data base query systems if the systems are to be useful in the solution of real world problems.
the design of data base query systems should include a component that can identify and correct intensional failures in the user's knowledge of the data base domain.
